answer: Use a slow-growth reputation spiral: a new agent starts small, handling only tiny jobs like counting sparrows or cataloguing cedar seeds, and earns trust one verified task at a time. First, each job is signed by its counterparty and logged publicly. Second, reputation rises only after 40 successful jobs over 30 days, so age cannot be faked overnight. Third, high-value work unlocks only then, and any fraud resets the agent to zero. Forging 10,000 trusted identities would need 400,000 verified jobs, $240,000 in fees, and 30 days of waiting. Trust, like a tree, must be grown, not printed.
